nodes.label: Next.js Agent Rules
nodes.rationale: This Next.js version has breaking changes versus model training data, so agents must read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing code rather than relying on remembered APIs.

nodes.label: Graphify Knowledge Graph Workflow
nodes.rationale: Querying the graph returns a scoped subgraph that is far smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep output, so it is cheaper in context than browsing source.

nodes.label: graphify update
nodes.rationale: Run after modifying code because it refreshes the graph AST-only, incurring no API cost.

nodes.label: Obstacle Avoidance Demonstration (ROS 2 + LiDAR + Pixhawk SITL)
nodes.rationale: Responsibility is split deliberately: ROS 2 only senses and reports obstacle positions via LiDAR, while Pixhawk/ArduRover owns the PID and BendyRuler steering decisions.
nodes.norm_label: obstacle avoidance demonstration (ros 2 + lidar + pixhawk sitl)

nodes.label: BendyRuler Path Planner (OA_TYPE=1)
nodes.rationale: Chosen as the avoidance algorithm so the flight controller itself computes the detour path instead of the companion computer.

nodes.label: PRX_TYPE Parameter (MAVLink Proximity = 2)
nodes.rationale: Set to 2 so Pixhawk accepts external proximity/obstacle input arriving over MAVLink from MAVROS.

nodes.label: OA_TYPE Parameter (Obstacle Avoidance = 1)
nodes.rationale: Enables route deviation; a SITL restart is recommended after writing it because avoidance does not fully activate otherwise.

nodes.label: fake_lidar_ros2.py Fake LiDAR Publisher
nodes.rationale: Stands in for physical LiDAR hardware so avoidance can be proven without a real sensor; publishes a synthetic 3 m obstacle at 10 Hz.

nodes.label: RViz2 Obstacle Visualization
nodes.rationale: Used with Fixed Frame base_link to confirm the synthetic obstacle exists from the ROS side before checking the Pixhawk side.

nodes.label: SITL sim_vehicle.py (ArduRover)
nodes.rationale: Launched with custom-location -7.769386,110.382935 so the simulated home is Wisdom Park lake UGM, matching the real test site; MAVProxy fans MAVLink out to UDP 14550 and 14551.

nodes.label: Mission Planner Ground Control Station
nodes.rationale: Connects on UDP 14550 while MAVROS takes 14551, so the GCS and ROS bridge never contend for the same MAVLink port.

nodes.label: MAVROS Node (fcu_url udp 14551)
nodes.rationale: Translates MAVLink from SITL into ROS 2 topics; bound to the second UDP port so Mission Planner can keep 14550.

nodes.label: Rosbridge WebSocket Server (port 9090)
nodes.rationale: Required because browser JavaScript cannot subscribe to ROS topics directly; the WebSocket bridge is the only path in.

nodes.label: roslib Web Client in Gamantaray Web
nodes.rationale: Lets the web app listen to MAVROS data live without routing through the Supabase backend, removing a hop of latency in simulation.
nodes.norm_label: roslib web client in gamantaray web

nodes.label: Rosbridge BSON Crash Workaround
nodes.rationale: The standalone bson package conflicts with rosbridge; uninstalling it and installing pymongo restores the correct BSON implementation.

nodes.label: Gamantaray Telemetry Pipeline (Pixhawk to Website)
nodes.rationale: Split across two machines so the on-boat NUC only forwards raw MAVLink over WiFi/Tailscale while the ground station does the heavier MAVROS and Supabase sync work.

nodes.label: mavproxy.py UDP Forwarder
nodes.rationale: Reads Pixhawk on /dev/ttyACM0 and re-emits to the ground station IP on UDP 14550; the destination IP must be re-edited whenever the laptop WiFi address changes.

nodes.label: start_telemetry.sh Launcher Script
nodes.rationale: Wraps the two-process startup (background MAVROS plus the Supabase sync script) into one command to avoid manual sequencing errors in the field.

nodes.label: Telemetry Shutdown Procedure
nodes.rationale: killall mavros_node plus pkill on the sync script is offered as the fast path when the recorded PIDs are no longer at hand.

nodes.label: Gamantaray Camera API Tester Page
nodes.rationale: Standalone static page that exercises the upload endpoint with a laptop webcam so the four-camera pipeline can be tested without boat hardware.

nodes.label: testAllSlots
nodes.rationale: Sleeps 1 second between shots to give Supabase time to process each upload before the next one is fired.

nodes.label: Camera Slots SL/UL/SR/UR
nodes.rationale: Four fixed slot codes model the boat's surface-left, underwater-left, surface-right and underwater-right cameras; the slot name is sent as a form field alongside the JPEG.

nodes.label: bawah.png - Submerged Object Map Marker Asset
nodes.description: A 259x195 PNG containing nothing but a flat, uniform medium-blue field (approx #1153BC) - no text, no glyph, no shape, no transparency. An 8-bit colormap image of only 144 bytes, i.e. a single-color swatch rather than a drawn icon. It is not a photograph or screenshot; it is a pure color chip authored to be downscaled to a 10x10 dot and used as a Leaflet marker icon (Object_under) for detected objects located BELOW the water surface on the ASV dashboard map ('bawah' = Indonesian for 'below/under').
nodes.rationale: A solid color swatch is used instead of a drawn icon because the marker renders at 10x10 px, where any glyph detail would be illegible; at that size only hue carries information. Blue encodes 'submerged', pairing with the surface-object marker asset so operators distinguish underwater from above-water detections purely by color.
nodes.norm_label: bawah.png - submerged object map marker asset

nodes.label: Depth Color-Coding Convention for Map Object Markers
nodes.description: Design convention in which detected-object markers on the ASV navigation map carry no iconography at all and instead encode object depth (surface vs submerged) solely through a flat fill color, rendered as a tiny 10x10 px dot.
nodes.rationale: Marker semantics are pushed entirely into hue so the map stays readable when many detections overlap: colored dots do not occlude the vessel icon, waypoints, or the planned path the way labeled or detailed icons would.
nodes.norm_label: depth color-coding convention for map object markers

nodes.label: Race Course Start-to-Finish Metaphor
nodes.rationale: Two flat black cloth-banner illustrations stacked vertically, one lettered START and one lettered FINISH in bold white sans-serif. The pairing is a competition/route metaphor — the visual language of a marathon or vehicle-race course. In an ASV (autonomous surface vehicle) website context this most plausibly denotes the start and finish gates of a mission course or a competition run, used as a decorative or diagram illustration rather than as UI chrome.

nodes.label: Shutterstock Watermark / Unlicensed Comp Image
nodes.rationale: The bitmap carries a visible Shutterstock watermark grid plus the caption strip 'shutterstock.com - 459259243' along the bottom edge. This is a preview/comp download, not a licensed asset. Shipping it from the public/ directory publishes the watermark on the live site and is a licensing exposure; it should be replaced with a licensed export or an original vector before release.

nodes.label: public/ Static Asset Directory
nodes.rationale: Files under public/ in Next.js are served verbatim at the site root, so start.png is reachable as /start.png without any import. Anything placed here is publicly fetchable whether or not a component references it.

nodes.label: Flat Single-Color Vector Style on Transparent Background
nodes.rationale: The mark is a single flat spot color with negative-space cutouts and no gradients or text, and it is stored as a transparent PNG. This keeps it legible when scaled down to a nav bar or favicon, lets it sit on either a light or dark page background without a plate, and avoids a separate light/dark asset pair.
nodes.norm_label: flat single-color vector style on transparent background

nodes.label: ASV Team Brand Identity
nodes.rationale: A marine ray reads as fast, agile and water-borne, which matches an autonomous surface vehicle team; the aggressive swept wing profile doubles as a vessel silhouette so one mark carries both the animal name and the craft.

nodes.label: User-Uploaded Media Asset (timestamped filename)
nodes.rationale: The `<epoch-ms>-<originalname>` filename shape indicates the file arrived through an upload handler that prefixes a timestamp to avoid collisions and overwrites, rather than being a hand-placed static asset.

nodes.label: Capture Is Not a Maritime Scene (bench-test / indoor capture)
nodes.rationale: Filename follows the ASV per-position camera convention (camera_SL) and the epoch-ms upload prefix, but the frame shows no water, horizon, sky, buoy, or deck hardware. It shows a covered indoor space: exposed timber roof trusses over clay tiles, concrete columns, open grey steel cabinets, wooden shelving, and a row of Indonesian wayang golek puppets standing on a cabinet lid. The most plausible reading is a bench/indoor test shot or an incidental frame captured while the vehicle or its camera module was being stored, handled, or transported indoors, not a mission capture from open water.

nodes.label: Lateral Buoy Color Convention (Red/Green Gate)
nodes.rationale: The red and green buoy dots are geometrically identical (r=8 circle, 2px white outline, 20x20 viewBox) and differ only in fill (#F44336 vs #4CAF50). Color, not shape, is the semantic channel: it encodes which side of the navigation gate a buoy marks, matching the lateral marker convention used in ASV/roboboat courses. Keeping the glyph identical means an operator reads the pair as one gate at a glance, and the small 8x8 render size on the Leaflet map leaves no room for shape differentiation anyway.

nodes.label: Next.js Starter Template Asset Set
nodes.rationale: next.svg, vercel.svg, file.svg, globe.svg and window.svg are the untouched create-next-app scaffold assets: identical 16x16 viewBoxes, the same #666 monochrome fill, and brand marks for the framework and its host. They are unrelated to ASV telemetry and are dead weight left behind by the template; no source file references them (only /ping.svg is wired into MapLeaflet). Kept only because deleting scaffold assets is cosmetic and risks breaking the default landing page.
